search_company_news.title: Apple (AAPL) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates
search_company_news.content:
This is CNBC's live coverage of Apple's 2026 third-quarter earnings.

Apple reported stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 22% increase in iPhone sales. But the company issued weak guidance for the current period, citing "supply constraints." The stock slid more than 6% in extended trading.

Here's how the company did versus LSEG consensus estimates:

Here's how Apple did in other key areas:

Net income climbed to $29.79 billion, or $2.02 per share, from $23.43 billion, or $1.57 per share, a year ago. Apple said earnings included 11 cents per share from tariff rebates. [...] The stock was fell 1.4% for the day to close at $333.43. It's the second straight day of slippage after the stock hit a record on Tuesday, when the company briefly crossed the $5 trillion market cap milestone for the first time.

Even with the drop, Apple shares are up about 23% for the year.

— Ari Levy

Apple has topped revenue and earnings estimates for 13 straight quarters, dating back to the period ended December 2022.

When the company last missed expectations, overall sales for the holiday quarter dropped 5%, the first year-over-year decline since 2019.

Cook said at the time that three factors hurt the results: a strong dollar, production issues in China affecting the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the overall macroeconomic environment. [...] — Kif Leswing

Apple's iPad sales declined 6% on an annual basis. The company blamed the weakness on a difficult comparison to last year's quarter, when sales of the devices surged due to a new low-cost iPad.

Revenue in the company's wearables and home category increased 6% on an annual basis to $4.9 billion, topping estimates.

— Kif Leswing

Apple's services division, which delivers hefty margins, continued its steady growth, posting a revenue increase of 12% during the quarter to over $30 billion, although it missed analyst estimates. Apple said the services performance was hurt by foreign exchange headwinds.

Apple highlighted growth from advertising, App Store, AppleCare warranties, music, video, cloud services, and payment services.

search_company_news.title: Microsoft (MSFT) Q2 earnings report 2026
search_company_news.content:
For the fiscal second quarter, which ended on Dec. 31, Microsoft's revenue grew 16.7% year over year, according to a statement. Net income, at $38.46 billion, or $5.16 per share, was up from $24.11 billion, or $3.23 per share, in the same quarter a year earlier. Adjusted earnings exclude impact from investments in OpenAI. The company's gross margin was the narrowest it's been in three years, coming in just over 68%.

Revenue from Azure and other cloud services grew 39%, compared with 40% growth in the fiscal first quarter. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount and CNBC had expected 39.4% and 38.9% growth, respectively. [...] The company reported $9.97 billion in other income, compared with other expense of $2.29 billion in the same quarter a year ago. The swing comes three months after OpenAI announced a restructuring that involved its for-profit arm becoming a public-benefit corporation. Microsoft saw a decrease in its proportionate ownership of OpenAI, yielding a dilution gain.

At year end, the company's commercial remaining performance obligation, a measurement of unearned revenue and amounts that will be recognized as revenue later, stood at $625 billion, up some 110%. That's thanks to OpenAI's $250 billion cloud commitment with Microsoft during the quarter. Microsoft said 45% of commercial remaining performance obligation is tied to OpenAI, with the remainder growing 28%. [...] In the past three months, Microsoft stock has fallen about 11%, while the S&P 500 index has gained 1%, with investors pondering the risk of generative AI models hurting the growth prospects for traditional software.

search_company_news.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) earnings Q3 2026
search_company_news.content:
In this article

Alphabet shares slumped more than 10% after the search giant reported a drop in free cash flow during the third quarter, in a worrying sign for the artificial intelligence trade.

Here's how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:

Revenue grew 25% from a year ago, but the company posted its first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years.

Net income fell to $26.17 billion, or $2.12 per share, down from $34.98 billion, or $2.87 per share, a year ago.

The Google parent reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion, which fell much further than the $2.70 billion expected by analysts. [...] "We are seeing extraordinary demand and strong growth from both AI labs, capital markets, financial service institutions, and enterprises," said Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian in his first public earnings call remarks.

Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, surpassing the $28.7 billion expected by analysts. The company has continued taking market share from larger rivals Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

The strong cloud results did little to shake off Google's largely negative print.

"The cloud business was the only business that beat at 103% growth," said Jefferies analyst Brent Thill on CNBC's Closing Bell: Overtime. "The Street wanted 100%, so it didn't beat by much, and it missed some of the high-end targets. Everything else missed." [...] The company's aggressive push on AI models did show signs of consumer adoption. Google said its Gemini app reached 1 billion users, making it the fastest-growing product in its history, the company said.

CEO Sundar Pichai told analysts that the company is already seeing strong demand for its recently launched Argon Gemini model. Its Carbon iteration announced on Wednesday outperforms Argon "on almost every domain," he added.

Alphabet's search revenue grew 12% to $63.35 billion. That fell short of a $64.96 billion estimate. Pichai said the company's AI investments powered the highest query growth rate over the last five years.

search_company_news.title: Alphabet Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
search_company_news.content:
## Google Cloud revenue more than doubles

Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion, driven by growth in Google Cloud Platform, AI infrastructure, AI solutions and core cloud services. TPU system sales were also a meaningful contributor, according to CFO Anat Ashkenazi. Cloud operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, and the segment's operating margin increased to 36.2% from 23.7% a year earlier.

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the business now has 18 product lines producing more than $1 billion each in annual revenue. Its backlog reached $561 billion, with Alphabet expecting to recognize just over 55% of that amount as revenue over the next 24 months. [...] Approaching Earnings Season, Are Pure Play Quantum Stocks Still a Good Bet?

Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% from a year earlier, as growth in Search, Google Cloud and subscriptions helped drive its 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth. CEO Sundar Pichai said the company had reached a half-trillion-dollar annual revenue run rate. [...] Capital expenditures totaled $51.4 billion in the third quarter, primarily for technical infrastructure supporting AI investments. Alphabet maintained its 2026 CapEx guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion and said it expects capital expenditures to increase significantly in 2027. Ashkenazi said the increased infrastructure investment will raise depreciation and data-center operating costs, while third-party computing capacity coming online in the fourth quarter is expected to create near-term Cloud margin headwinds.

Alphabet ended the quarter with $265.1 billion in cash and marketable securities and $125.1 billion in long-term debt. The board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share, payable in December.

•Net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion in the third quarter, compared with $180.2 billion in third quarter 2025. Excluding the $0.9 billion unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates throughout the quarter, net sales increased 13% compared with third quarter 2025. As a reminder, Prime Day timing shifted this year, with the event occurring in Q2 for most large countries. In 2025, Prime Day occurred entirely in Q3. Excluding this shift, third quarter year-over-year growth would have been approximately 400 basis points higher.

Third-quarter net income came in at $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, vs. $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year ago. The company said the decrease was driven primarily by a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain from its investment in the AI startup Anthropic, which was recorded in the 2025 third quarter.

While the AWS segment continues to hum along, results weren't as bright in Amazon's retail business, which remains its largest unit by revenue, or its advertising segment.

Online sales gained 2% year over year to $68.47 billion, which fell short of analysts' projected $69.68 billion, according to StreetAccount. It marked a slowdown from one year ago, when sales increased nearly 10%. [...] The aggressive AI spending has eaten into Amazon's cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, recording an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve month period, a swing of 386% year over year. In the prior quarter, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion.

The company said the shortfall was primarily due to an increase in purchases of property and equipment as a result of AI investments.

Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the quarter, ticking up from $35.1 billion one year earlier, and coming in well above analysts' estimated $58.7 billion, according to FactSet. [...] In this article

## Amazon Invests Another $1.9 Billion in the Delivery Service Partner Program with New Safety Initiatives and AI-Powered Technology

Amazon (AMZN) will invest another $1.9 billion in its Delivery Service Partner (DSP) program in 2027 to support DSP owners and help raise Delivery Associate (DA) pay to a national average of nearly $24 per hour.

Across the eight-year history of the program, Amazon has invested $21.7 billion to support DSPs and their drivers. Since 2022, it has spent more than $543 million on safety initiatives and technology, contributing to a reduction of serious vehicle crashes by more than 23% across the delivery network last year. Over the past three years, program investments are expected to have helped increase DA pay by an average of 16% nationwide. [...] Amazon is launching Day 1 Financial, a lifetime membership at First Tech Federal Credit Union for qualified employees and their families, with $0 overdraft and maintenance fees, no account minimums, and credit-building tools, rolling out from late 2026 into 2027. From October 1, 2026, every U.S. Amazon employee will receive an uncapped 10% discount on eligible groceries and essentials online and 20% off in-store at Whole Foods Market, on top of existing healthcare, free Prime, education, and retirement benefits.

search_company_news.title: Meta (META) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates
search_company_news.content:
This is CNBC's live coverage of Meta's 2026 third-quarter earnings.

Meta reported better-than-expected revenue in its third-quarter earnings report on Wednesday and issued strong guidance for the current period. The stock rose about 2.5% in extended trading.

It's not clear if earnings were comparable to the $5.75 per share expected by analysts.

Revenue jumped 26% from a year ago.

"We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model," said CEO Mark Zuckerberg in the earnings release.

For the fourth quarter, Meta said it expects revenue of between $73 billion and $76 billion, or $74.5 billion at the middle of the range. Analysts expected $73.73 billion, according to LSEG. [...] —Jonathan Vanian

Meta's Reality Labs division, which is tasked with developing virtual reality headsets and AI-powered wearable devices, is expected to post a loss of $4.54 billion while generating $513 million in sales for the third quarter, according to StreetAccount.

In July when Meta reported second-quarter earnings, the company revealed that the Reality Labs unit lost $4.62 billion while bringing in $431 million during the period.

With the VR market struggling to catch on with consumers, Zuckerberg has since shifted Reality Labs resources to center on more on AI-driven hardware products like the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses the company creates with eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica. [...] — Jonathan Vanian

Meta is offering $20 and $100 monthly subscription plans for Muse AI agent power users. Right now, Muse is free to use but requires a subscription to run it with Meta's latest model — Muse Wonder. The company is also charging developers $50 or $200 a month to access its most powerful Muse Wonder Full AI model via the Muse coding agent that debuted in early August.

Meta's nascent subscription efforts represent opportunities for the company to expand beyond online advertising, which is still its core money maker. Investors have been concerned about the Facebook parent's hefty AI investments relative to rivals like Alphabet and Amazon that have cloud computing businesses.

search_company_news.content:
Posted: 2026-10-21
Meta Platforms boosted its capital spending outlook and announced plans for a new class of nonvoting stock, escalating its already-stratospheric bet on artificial intelligence. Capital expenditures will be $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, the social-media giant said during its quarterly earnings report Wednesday, raising the bottom end of the range from $130 billion. The new class of shares, meanwhile, will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January. About TSLA

Tesla, Inc. engages in the design, development, manufacture, and sale of electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems. It operates through the Automotive and Energy Generation and Storage segments. The Automotive segment includes the design, development, manufacture, sale, and lease of electric vehicles as well as sales of automotive regulatory credits. The Energy Generation and Storage segment is involved in the design, manufacture, installation, sale, and lease of solar energy generation, energy storage products, and related services and sales of solar energy systems incentives. The company was founded by Jeffrey B. Straubel, Elon Reeve Musk, Martin Eberhard, and Marc Tarpenning on July 1, 2003 and is headquartered in Austin, TX.

search_company_news.content:
Net income attributable to common share holders plummeted 29% to $787 million, or 22 cents a share, from $1.11 billion, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier, Tesla said.

The drop in profitability reflects a surge in spending on Optimus humanoid robots and other artificial intelligence initiatives. Capital expenditures more than doubled from a year earlier to $3.73 billion. Free cash flow plunged by 62% year over year to $1.53 billion, after Tesla turned free cash flow negative in the second quarter.

Tesla said uptake of its FSD (Supervised), a partially automated driving system the company sells for $99 per month in the U.S., grew by 20 percentage points from the second quarter. Active FSD subscriptions increased 67% from a year earlier to 1.74 million. [...] "I think I said everything that should be said yesterday," he said.

Tesla's revenue was down slightly flat from a year earlier, when the company generated sales of $28.24 billion, according to the earnings deck. In Tesla's core automotive business, revenue declined 3% from a year earlier to $20.56 billion in the quarter. Energy revenue fell 16% to $2.88 billion.

Balancing out the declines were gains in Tesla's services and other revenue. Sales there climbed 33% from a year ago to $4.61 billion.

Tesla blamed its lackluster automotive revenue and profits on lower average sales prices for its cars during the quarter, and trouble securing battery supplies to make enough vehicles to fulfill a backlog of orders. [...] "We believe that FSD is driving demand in markets where it is available, and we continue to work with regulators to get it approved in other markets," the company said in its investor deck.

Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's vice president of Autopilot, said on the earnings call that the company plans to give some customer cars access to its forthcoming FSD (Unsupervised) systems around the second quarter of next year.

Tesla is testing its Cybercab, a bronze two-seater designed for use as a robotaxi, but it's not yet sold to individuals. Musk said on the call that "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and transport-as-a-service."

# JPMorgan Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Capital Deployment and AI Risks

Zacks Equity Research

4 min read

 JPM

  +1.21%

JPMorgan Chase & Co. JPM emphasized organic capital deployment, resilient business activity and cautious risk management during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management also outlined expectations for higher net interest income in 2027 while acknowledging uncertainty surrounding interest rates and economic conditions.

The bank reported adjusted earnings of $5.75 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.94 by 3.2%. Reported revenues of $50.17 billion also fell short of the consensus estimate of $52.21 billion by 3.9%.

### JPMorgan Chase & Co. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise [...] Consumer & Community Banking revenues advanced 9% to $21.2 billion. Debit and credit-card spending increased 10%, while the bank added more than 650,000 net new checking accounts. Management described consumer finances as resilient, supported by employment conditions.

## JPM Weighs Credit Risks Against Growth Opportunities

Credit conditions remained an important focus as analysts questioned the implications of sustained higher borrowing costs.

Responding to a KBW analyst, Dimon indicated that JPMorgan was tightening certain lending standards, citing weaker covenants and aggressive financing structures. Barnum maintained that corporate balance sheets remained generally sound. [...] Dimon reinforced restrictions on external AI agents accessing internal systems. Barnum also acknowledged that productivity benefits from generative AI remain difficult to identify in quarterly financial results, despite encouraging internal experimentation.

## JPMorgan Sees Strong Equities and Consumer Activity

Commercial & Investment Bank revenues increased 14% year over year to $22.7 billion, supported by investment banking, payments and equities activity.

Barnum highlighted a 49% increase in Equity Markets revenues, contrasting with a 4% decline in Fixed Income Markets. Investment banking fees rose 14%, although management noted some moderation in transaction activity amid bond-market volatility.

With fiscal year 2025 revenue of $681 billion, Walmart employs approximately 2.1 million associates worldwide. Walmart continues to be a leader in sustainability, corporate philanthropy, and employment opportunity.

search_company_news.content:
For the three-month period ended July 31, Walmart reported net income of $6.37 billion, or 80 cents per share, compared with $7.03 billion, or 88 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Excluding the impact of a loss on investments and including a benefit from what it called a tax matter, Walmart reported adjusted earnings per share of 81 cents. The company's gross profit rate grew to 25.4%, boosted by the tariff refund benefit.

Total revenue climbed to $187.94 billion from $177.40 billion in the year-earlier period. [...] Shares of Walmart closed about 9% lower Thursday, as Wall Street appeared disappointed by the quarterly comparable sales and the company's sales guidance.

For the third quarter, Walmart said it expects net sales to increase between 3% and 3.75% and adjusted earnings per share to be between 62 cents and 64 cents.

The retailer expects net sales to increase between 4% and 5% for the year, compared with a previous outlook of between 3.5% and 4.5% growth. Walmart also anticipates adjusted earnings will be between $2.80 and $2.87 per share, compared with the prior guidance of between $2.75 and $2.85 per share. [...] In this article

Walmart on Thursday posted quarterly sales that beat Wall Street estimates and raised its outlook for the year, as it saw another strong quarter of e-commerce growth and benefited from tariff refunds.

"Our business is strong," CFO John David Rainey told CNBC. "We feel really good about the progress we're making."

The retailer said revenue rose 5.9% in its fiscal second quarter as e-commerce sales jumped 23% globally. Walmart also said U.S. comparable sales grew 2.6%, offset in part by a 0.8% headwind in its health and wellness business as price caps on certain drugs took effect. That was less than the 3.5% increase Wall Street expected, according to FactSet.

search_company_news.content:
Walmart WMT 1.76%increase; up pointing triangle reported its smallest sales gain in more than six years as some Americans continue to spend cautiously—especially when shopping at the retailer’s physical stores.

On Thursday, Walmart said U.S. comparable sales, those from store and digital channels operating for the past 12 months, rose 2.6%. That is the smallest quarterly increase the retailer has reported since 2020. The number was hurt by new pharmacy-pricing regulations, without which Walmart would have had a 3.4% lift, the company said. That is below analysts’ estimates of a 3.8% gain, according to FactSet.

J&J raised its full-year forecast for reported sales to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, up from $101.1 billion. It increased its adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 per share, up from $11.04.

Quarterly pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% to $16.76 billion.

Sales of Tremfya for Crohn's disease and other autoimmune conditions rose 68% to $2.4 billion, exceeding analyst estimates of about $2.2 billion, while sales of Stelara, which is facing generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above diminished Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Johnson & Johnson reported sales in its medical devices business on Tuesday that fell short of Wall Street expectations, citing geopolitical issues, including the Middle East conflict, and its shares fell more than 6%.

The results marked the second successive quarter that its MedTech unit missed analysts' estimates.

Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said in an interview that the Middle East conflict, austerity measures in Europe, and pricing in China continued to weigh on international results in the third quarter, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way."

The Middle East conflict, which has driven up fuel costs, has not yet affected the company's costs, he said, but it has hurt sales in the region.

Business News›News›International›US News›SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. # SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. SoFi Technologies stock saw a 7% climb due to Trump's tax plan. The plan limits federal student loans, potentially benefiting private lenders like SoFi. Investors are optimistic, with the stock up over 100% in three months. SoFi's Q2 results are due on July 29. SoFi Technologies stock climbed 7% on Tuesday as investors responded to the latest policy changes proposed by US president Donald Trump, as per a report. His recently signed tax plan into law includes new limits on federal student loans, a move that could shift more borrowers toward private lenders like SoFi, and markets are taking notice, according to a TipRanks report. That gap in funding could create an opening for private loan providers, and SoFi, long known for its student loan and refinancing business, is well-positioned to benefit, as per the report. The market sees an opportunity for growth for the company, as a drop in federal support could drive more borrowers to its platform, and that’s what investors are betting on, according to the TipRanks report. SoFi stock has now increased more than 100% in the past three months, as reported by TipRanks. ## Earnings Buzz Builds Ahead of July 29 Report. The firm's stock rise comes as SoFi is going to post its second-quarter results on July 29, and investor expectations are already high, as reported by TipRanks. As per the TipRanks report, Wall Street analysts projected that the company will report earnings of $0.06 per share, increasing 500% from the year-ago quarter. With student lending now in focus because of Trump's tax bill, SoFi’s performance in that segment is expected to draw even closer attention this quarter, and a solid report might give the firm's stock another lift as "policy tailwinds and strong business fundamentals begin to align," wrote TipRanks in its report.

Title: SoFi Stock Forecast 2026: Latest News, Earnings, Risks and SOFI Price Prediction - zinpedia
## SoFi Stock Forecast 2026: Latest News, Earnings, Risks and SOFI Price Prediction. SoFi Technologies has grown from a student-loan refinancing company into a broad digital financial-services business. Today, its platform includes lending, banking, investing, credit cards and financial technology infrastructure. That wider business model has made **SoFi stock**, traded on Nasdaq under the ticker **SOFI**, popular among growth investors. Supporters see a fast-growing digital bank with rising membership, expanding revenue and improving profitability. Critics argue that the stock already reflects a large amount of future growth and remains exposed to credit conditions, interest rates, regulation and competition. As of July 24, 2026, SOFI shares were trading near $16.59, giving the company a market value of approximately $22.9 billion. Its trailing price-to-earnings ratio was around 36.9, based on the latest available market data. The question for investors is therefore not simply whether SoFi is growing. The more important question is whether the company can grow fast enough—and profitably enough—to justify its valuation. This article examines the latest SoFi stock news, financial results, growth drivers, risks, and a scenario-based price prediction for 2026. It is not personalized financial advice, and no stock-price forecast is guaranteed. ## What Is SoFi Technologies and How Does It Make Money? SoFi Technologies is a digital financial-services company and bank holding company. Through SoFi Bank and its broader technology platform, it offers products that help customers borrow, save, spend, and invest money. Lending has historically generated a large share of SoFi’s revenue. This part of the company is important because it allows SoFi to build longer relationships with members. The company reported that Financial Services products reached approximately 19.3 million in the first quarter of 2026. The Technology Platform gives SoFi an opportunity to earn business-to-business revenue rather than depending entirely on consumer loans and banking products. First-quarter 2026 Technology Platform revenue fell 27% year over year to approximately $75.1 million, partly because a large client completed its transition away from the platform before the end of 2025. SoFi reported strong operating results for the first quarter of 2026. The company also stated that its Loan Platform Business is able to make fee income from originating loans for partners and keeping the servicing rights.

SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. – (BUSINESS WIRE) – October 27, 2026 – SoFi Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: SOFI), a member-centric, everything app for digital financial services that helps members borrow, save, spend, invest and protect their money, reported financial results today for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. [...] Member and Product Growth

Continued growth in both total members and products in the third quarter is the result of our continued investments in innovation and brand building and reflects the benefits of our broad product suite and unique FSPL strategy. SoFi has reached significant scale whereby member growth, product growth, and revenue per product are key drivers of business performance.

SoFi added a record 1.2 million members in the third quarter of 2026, bringing total members to 17.1 million, up 35% from 12.6 million at the end of the same prior year period.

SoFi also achieved record product additions of 2.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, bringing total products to nearly 26.7 million, up 44% from 18.6 million at the end of the same prior year period. [...] Earnings Webcast

SoFi’s executive management team will host a live audio webcast beginning at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time (5:00 a.m. Pacific Time) today to discuss the quarter’s financial results and business highlights. search_company_news.title: Roku stock surges on earnings beat, record premium subscriptions
search_company_news.content:
Analysts at Rosenblatt Securities on Friday upgraded Roku's stock to buy from neutral, citing the strong fourth-quarter results and several potential growth levers for the company in the near term.

"Big picture — Roku has built a formidable gatekeeper presence for U.S. streaming — half of all streaming in the U.S. on TVs goes through their devices," the analysts wrote.

Rosenblatt noted the improved ability to monetize streaming with its partnership with Amazon, a new ad tool for small and mid-sized businesses and tweaks made to the front page for advanced ads.

Correction: Roku reported fourth-quarter earnings of 53 cents per share. An earlier version mischaracterized the figure. [...] For the current period, Roku said it expects to report $1.2 billion in revenue, which is higher than the $1.16 billion expected by analysts, according to StreetAccount. It also projected full-year revenue of $5.5 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $5.34 billion, according to StreetAccount.

Last May, Roku acquired Frndly, a live TV subscription streaming service, for $185 million. The company also recently launched an ad-free streaming service, called Howdy, that costs $2.99 a month.

Wood told investors on the company's earnings call that Howdy has the potential to become a "very large service" over time. Roku also said it's on track to surpass 100 million streaming households this year. [...] Roku executives said in their shareholder letter that the fourth quarter was the "biggest quarter ever" for net adds to premium subscriptions. The program lets users subscribe to different streaming services, like HBO Max and Paramount+, using a single login on the Roku platform.

The company said it expects to roll out premium subscription bundles this year.

Revenue grew 18% from $1.03 billion a year ago. Net income totaled $80.5 million, or 53 cents per share, compared with a loss of $35.5 million, or 24 cents a share, one year earlier.

Lucid (NASDAQ: LCID) reported Q2 2026 revenue of $405 million, up 56% year over year, with production of 4,774 vehicles (+24%) and deliveries of 3,953 (+19%). Net loss was $1.03 billion, and the company ended the quarter with $3.0 billion in total liquidity, which, along with recently secured financing, is expected to provide runway well into 2027.

Lucid launched an operational reset centered on cash, customers and culture, including a $1.4 billion 2026 cash flow improvement plan across inventory, capex and opex, underpinned by June’s U.S. workforce reduction. Priority projects include the Uber/Nuro robotaxi program (nearly 100 test vehicles), industrialization of the Saudi AMP‑2 plant, and continued development of its midsize program. [...] For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, production totaled 2,954 vehicles. Deliveries exceeded production as existing inventory moved to customers. Production declined sequentially following the elimination of a second shift at AMP-1 in June. Lucid said it continued aligning production with near-term demand and that demand for the Lucid Gravity continued to regain momentum.

search_company_news.title: Nio's Sales Are Rising but 18.5% Is the Key Number to Watch When Q3 Earnings Arrive | The Motley Fool
search_company_news.content:
Nio ES9

Nio's ES9. Image source: Nio.

But there is a bit of a catch. Management also highlighted rising costs for memory chips, batteries, and other materials. Its stated aim during the earnings call was to keep third- and fourth-quarter vehicle margins around the second-quarter level.

Investors shouldn't treat another sequential margin increase as a given. Holding near 18.5% would still represent meaningful improvement from the 14.7% recorded in last year's third quarter⁠. Sometimes holding your ground is still progress, especially when costs are driving in the opposite direction.

## NIO - Nio

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/29/26

### Key data points

## What investors should watch [...] The Motley Fool
The Motley Fool

For Nio (NIO +0.00%) investors, selling more vehicles is encouraging, especially as it needs scale to break even for the full year 2026, as management has targeted. But turning those sales into sustainable profits? That's where the automotive industry gets challenging.

The electric vehicle (EV) maker delivered 109,178 vehicles during the third quarter, increasing 25.4% year over year, according to its delivery update⁠. That's solid growth, but investors already know the delivery total. The upcoming earnings report needs to tell us more about the financial quality of those sales.

One figure deserves particular attention: vehicle margin. Nio has made substantial progress on that front, and protecting those gains could matter more than investors realize. [...] ### Key data points

## What investors should watch

Nio needs more than growing sales to establish sustainable company-wide profitability. It needs to continue controlling costs and managing incentives amid a brutal Chinese auto price war. Its second-quarter results emphasize the remaining gap between GAAP and adjusted figures: Nio reported an operating loss of approximately RMB347 million, although adjusted operating profit, which excludes certain items, was approximately RMB207 million.

# Beyond Meat (NASDAQ:BYND) Surprises With Q2 CY2026 Sales, Provides Optimistic Revenue Guidance for Next Quarter

### Radek Strnad/

August 5, 2026

Plant-based protein company Beyond Meat (NASDAQ:BYND) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q2 CY2026, but sales fell by 8.2% year on year to $68.83 million. On top of that, next quarter’s revenue guidance ($62.5 million at the midpoint) was surprisingly good and 4.9% above what analysts were expecting. Its non-GAAP loss of $0.09 per share was 13.3% below analysts’ consensus estimates. [...] Is now the time to buy Beyond Meat? Find out in our full research report.

### Beyond Meat (BYND) Q2 CY2026 Highlights:

 Revenue: $68.83 million vs analyst estimates of $60.77 million (8.2% year-on-year decline, 13.3% beat)
 Adjusted EPS: -$0.09 vs analyst expectations of -$0.08 (13.3% miss)
 Adjusted EBITDA: -$27.7 million (-40.2% margin, 25.2% year-on-year decline)
 Revenue Guidance for Q3 CY2026 is $62.5 million at the midpoint, above analyst estimates of $59.58 million
 Operating Margin: -44.8%, up from -50% in the same quarter last year
 Free Cash Flow was -$19.62 million compared to -$33.77 million in the same quarter last year
 Sales Volumes fell 9.5% year on year (-18.9% in the same quarter last year)
 Market Capitalization: $326.6 million

### Company Overview [...] In Beyond Meat’s Q2 2026, sales volumes dropped 9.5% year on year. This result represents a further deceleration from its historical levels, showing the business is struggling to move its products.

## Key Takeaways from Beyond Meat’s Q2 Results

We were impressed by how significantly Beyond Meat blew past analysts’ revenue expectations this quarter. We were also glad its revenue guidance for next quarter exceeded Wall Street’s estimates. On the other hand, its EBITDA missed and its EPS fell short of Wall Street’s estimates. Overall, this was a softer quarter. The stock traded up 1.8% to $0.63 immediately following the results.

search_company_news.title: 3 Huge Red Flags From Tilray's Q1 Earnings Report | The Motley Fool
search_company_news.content:
The Motley Fool
The Motley Fool

Last week, Tilray Brands (TLRY -4.17%) reported its first-quarter numbers for fiscal 2027. While management boasted of its record-breaking numbers and diversified business, investors shouldn't buy the hype at all.

Tilray has been a bad investment for many years, and acquisitions may have boosted its revenue, but they haven't changed the story around this troubling marijuana stock. It's a bad buy, and the three numbers below from its earnings report only confirm that.

Stressed man at an office desk watches a falling stock market chart on his computer.

Image source: Getty Images.

## Tilray's cash burn spiked to more than $16.5 million [...] Tilray's operating expenses totaled $101.6 million this past quarter, which is an increase of 83% from the same period last year. That is, however, with the company getting a $15 million benefit from the change in the fair value of contingent consideration a year ago. If that's removed, then the year-over-year increase in operating expense is 44%. But that's still higher than the company's top-line growth.

With a more bloated business, Tilray's actually going in the opposite direction of its peers, Canopy Growth and Aurora Cannabis, which have been looking to get leaner. It's not a strategy I think will end up paying off for Tilray.

## TLRY - Tilray Brands

NASDAQ · As of 5:00 PM ET 10/30/26

### Key data points

## Tilray's decline isn't likely to end anytime soon [...] ## Tilray's decline isn't likely to end anytime soon

Despite top-line growth, the market didn't appear impressed with Tilray's latest numbers, as the stock has fallen since it posted them. Unfortunately, I don't see a path for the stock to get out of its tailspin anytime soon. It's a stock that's full of risk and that investors are likely better off avoiding.

search_company_news.content:
During its quarterly call with investors, Lyft CFO Erin Brewer said the figure was incorrect and that the actual increase will be 50 basis points, or 0.5%. That means Lyft's adjusted profit margin as a percentage of bookings will be 2.1% this year, up from 1.6% in 2023. The mistake also appeared in Lyft's slide deck.

"Look, it was a bad error, and that's on me," Risher said Wednesday.

The stock was still up after the correction, because the numbers beat analysts' estimates, but it lost much of its initial pop, equal to over $2 billion in market cap.

"We had thousands of eyes, we've got a process on this that is nuts," Risher said. "It's a terrible thing. It is an extra zero that slipped into a press release." [...] Risher said the company discovered the error after it became clear on the earnings call that there was a lot of interest in the margin. When a team member identified the problem, Risher said he could see her "jaw drop."

"Thank goodness we caught it pretty fast, and we issued an immediate correction," he said.

Lyft shares jumped 35% on Wednesday to $16.09, their best day since the company's IPO in 2019. However, the stock is still about 77% below its debut price.

Lyft reported $1.22 billion in revenue for the quarter, an increase of 4% from $1.175 billion a year earlier. The company posted adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, which was above the 8 cents expected by analysts, according to LSEG, formerly known as Refinitiv. [...] In this article

Lyft CEO David Risher took responsibility for the major error that appeared in the company's fourth-quarter earnings release, telling CNBC's "Squawk Box" that it's "super frustrating" for everyone on the team.

Shares of the ride-hailing company soared more than 60% after the report came out late Tuesday because the press release said Lyft would see margin expansion of 500 basis points, or 5%, in 2024, a huge increase for a business that has long struggled to turn a profit.

search_company_news.content:
Prices move sharply and unpredictably. Microsoft and Meta both reported on 29 July 2026. Nvidia reported a month later, on 26 August 2026. Microsoft rose and Meta fell sharply in extended trading, and Nvidia moved sharply the following session.
 Unexpected one-off charges distort a single quarter. Meta's Q2 2026 report stated they record $2.40 billion legal charge and $1.18 billion of severance, these figures make the company appear to be a struggling business. Charges like these cut both ways, and their absence can easily make an otherwise weak quarterly performance appear better. [...] 1. Adjusted Earnings and Long-Term Trends

 

The other reason is you have to actually read the adjusted number rather than just accept it as it is. For its fiscal fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026, Microsoft reported GAAP diluted EPS of $4.81 and non-GAAP EPS of $4.74. The $0.07 difference came from marking its OpenAI investment to market, roughly $480 million that moved through reported earnings without any cash changing hands. Neither figure is wrong, and comparing one company's adjusted number against another's GAAP number produces nonsense.

 

Analyzing multiple reports each year will demonstrate whether a business is truly experiencing cumulative growth or merely stagnating without significant progress.

 

## What Are the Risks and Things to Watch?

search_company_news.title: I Was Wrong About Meta Earnings, But the Stock Is Still a Buy | The Motley Fool
search_company_news.content:
The Motley Fool
The Motley Fool

Meta Platforms (META -1.53%) tumbled on its second-quarter earnings report Wednesday.

The stock was down more than 10% at one point after hours, as it badly missed bottom-line estimates, with expenses jumping in part due to one-time costs for legal proceedings and severance payments.

Earnings per share fell from $7.14 to $6.18, well below the consensus at $7.22.

I predicted Meta Platforms would spike on the report, but that didn't happen. The company delivered strong results on the top line, with revenue up 28% to $60.8 billion, beating estimates at $60.3 billion, as the core advertising business drove 14% growth in ad impressions and a 12% increase in average price per ad. [...] However, investors were understandably more focused on falling profits and its capital expenditures, which are now expected to be $130 billion-$145 billion, as free cash flow in the quarter was less than $1 billion, including payments on finance leases. Management also did little to assuage concerns about overspending on capex, saying that it saw a "massive" opportunity in AI.

Management also seemed less enthusiastic about its new cloud business than investors had hoped, as the company still prefers to use its AI chips internally, where it says it gets a higher return on investment.

Social media icons floating up from a smartphone.

Image source: Getty Images.

## Why the stock could bounce back [...] NASDAQ · As of 5:00 PM ET 10/30/26

### Key data points

If the after-hours pullback holds, Meta stock will be trading at a price-to-earnings ratio of just 21, and adjusting for one-time tax penalties, it trades at a P/E of just 18. That's an unbelievable bargain for a company expected to continue growing revenue by more than 20%.

At this point, it seems that investors are betting that Meta's AI investments won't deliver any returns, but that's a low bar for the company to overcome, and it creates substantial upside potential if they do pay off. There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions. [...] Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for FiscalNote Holdings, Inc. was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is -$0.59 on $22.62 million in revenues for the coming quarter and -$1.83 on $92.81 million in revenues for the current fiscal year. [...] This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +1.01%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post a loss of $0.84 per share when it actually produced a loss of $1.73, delivering a surprise of -105.95%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times.

FiscalNote Holdings, Inc., which belongs to the Zacks Technology Services industry, posted revenues of $22.2 million for the quarter ended December 2025, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.84%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $29.47 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates two times over the last four quarters.

## Market backdrop

Tech stocks swung sharply last week as investors stepped up scrutiny of the AI trade, pushing the Nasdaq down roughly 1% despite strong earnings from some of the sector’s biggest names. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, with a rotation into defensive sectors helping limit losses. U.S. 10-year Treasury yields slipped below 5% as investors sought refuge from the tech selloff. Brent crude oil touched a six-month high of $117 a barrel on concerns about further disruption to Middle East energy flows. [...] | Spain | We are overweight. Valuations remain attractive vs. peers even if relative earnings momentum has slowed. Strong domestic demand growth and exposure to fast-growing areas like Latin America support Spanish stocks. Financials, utilities and infrastructure-linked stocks would benefit from Europe’s push towards autonomy. |
| Netherlands | We are neutral. Earnings revisions in the IT sector, a large sector in the Dutch stock market is offset by other sectors seeing less favorable valuations and a weaker earnings outlook than European peers. | [...] | Emerging markets (EM) |  | We are overweight. Strong earnings and cheaper valuations create opportunities. We particularly like different expressions of the AI scarcity theme across Asia and Latin America. |
| China |  | We are neutral. We see opportunities in physical AI. Cheap, open-source AI could drive adoption, but that doesn’t necessarily translate into AI-provider profitability. |

| Short U.S. Treasuries |  | We are overweight. Much of the repricing we anticipated has occurred, and expectations for further Fed hikes look excessive. We favor the front end for attractive income and a greater breakeven buffer. |

search_company_news.title: Nurix Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter Fiscal 2023 Financial Results and Provides a Corporate Update | Nurix Therapeutics, Inc.
search_company_news.content:
Nurix announced a first of its kind strategic collaboration with Seagen: In September, Nurix entered a collaboration with Seagen to develop a portfolio of Degrader-Antibody Conjugates (DACs): antibodies that deliver a targeted protein degrader payload to selectively kill cancer cells. Nurix received a $60 million upfront payment and has the potential to receive approximately $3.4 billion in milestone payments plus future royalties. Nurix also retains an option for U.S. profit sharing and co-promotion on two products arising from the collaboration. In addition, Nurix announced that with the receipt of the $60 million upfront payment, Nurix expects that its existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, excluding any future potential milestones from collaborations, will be [...] SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 12, 2023 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nurix Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: NRIX), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing targeted protein modulation drugs designed to treat patients with hematologic malignancies and solid tumors, today reported financial results for the fiscal quarter ended August 31, 2023, and provided a corporate update. [...] “As our drug development pipeline continues to advance in the clinic, we are excited to add to our pipeline with Seagen to advance a portfolio of Degrader-Antibody Conjugates, or DACs, a new class of highly selective cancer therapeutics,” said Arthur T. Sands, M.D., Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of Nurix. “Nurix enters the fourth quarter of 2023 in a strong financial position due to our ability to access significant revenue from corporate partners including our recently announced agreement with Seagen and ongoing strategic collaborations with Gilead and Sanofi.”
